## Why This Is Asked
Interviews probe capability to apply 3-valued logic to practical policy constraints and design a backtracking propagator to verify satisfiability with Unknowns.

## Key Concepts
- 3-valued logic semantics and implication
- Backtracking propagation for unknowns
- Constraint satisfaction with Unknowns in policy contexts

## Code Example
```javascript
// 3-valued logic helpers (Kleene)
const NOT = v => v === 'T' ? 'F' : v === 'F' ? 'T' : 'U';
const OR = (x,y) => x === 'T' || y === 'T' ? 'T' : x === 'U' || y === 'U' ? 'U' : 'F';
const IMP = (p,q) => OR(NOT(p), q);
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How does backtracking scale with more fields?
- What if you require at least two U? How would constraints adapt?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to reason through 3-valued logic on a cyclical constraint graph and to design propagation/backtracking without exhaustive search.

## Key Concepts
- Kleene three-valued logic and implication as ¬A ∨ B
- Cycle constraints and propagation across a loop
- Strategy to avoid forcing any constraint to F while ensuring at least one U

## Code Example
```javascript
function neg(v){ if(v==='T') return 'F'; if(v==='F') return 'T'; return 'U'; }
function or(a,b){ const rank={F:0,U:1,T:2}; return rank[a] >= rank[b] ? a : b; }
function implies(a,b){ return or(neg(a), b); }
const X = {X1:'U', X2:'F', X3:'T', X4:'T'};
console.log([implies(X.X1,X.X2), implies(X.X2,X.X3), implies(X.X3,X.X4), implies(X.X4,X.X1)]);
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend to n variables in a cycle and detect unsatisfiable cases efficiently?
- How does propagation change if you allow two constraints to be evaluated as indeterminate rather than simply not-F?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests applying 3-valued Kleene logic to practical constraint propagation in a realistic, beginner-friendly scenario.

## Key Concepts
- Kleene 3-valued semantics: ¬T=F, ¬F=T, ¬U=U; ∧/∨ use T>U>F; P→Q as (¬P) ∨ Q.
- Backtracking propagator: pick a U, propagate through implications, backtrack if a constraint forces F.
- Constructive example: show a concrete assignment with at least one U and no F.

## Code Example
```javascript
function not(v){return v==='T'?'F':v==='F'?'T':'U';}
function or(a,b){const order={F:0,U:1,T:2}; return order[a] >= order[b] ? a : b;}
function and(a,b){const order={F:0,U:1,T:2}; return order[a] <= order[b] ? a : b;}
function implies(p,q){return or(not(p), q);} // Kleene-style
```
